name: frontend
description: Build maintainable, domain-modular React UI applications, plus thin architecture-routing adapters for Vue.js and Angular (stack detection, greenfield/existing routing, and the three-zone model translated into each framework's vocabulary — no naming/data-layer/testing/bootstrap depth yet for either, unlike the React adapter). Next.js needs no separate adapter: it's a React meta-framework the React adapter's own stack profiling already detects. React's greenfield default is Vite + React Router + RTK Query + shadcn/ui + Vitest, but it profiles what a project actually uses first — meta-framework, router, server-state library, and whether it's even a web app rather than a Remotion or React Native codebase — and translates its stack-independent rules into the libraries already installed instead of proposing a migration. Testing covers unit (Vitest) and integration (RTL + MSW) only — no browser-driven tests at any depth; a sibling e2e-testing plugin is the sole home for every Playwright test in this marketplace, from a five-minute smoke check to a full cross-stack workflow, and owns the @playwright/test dependency itself. Includes a thin React adapter over the framework-neutral UI architecture, RTK-Query-based data layer, module-scoped context, typed routing, greenfield project bootstrap with Tailwind and the theme file wired in from the first commit, file naming conventions, an installable shadcn/ui component library, component composition/non-duplication guidance, and React best practices — plus a framework-neutral Vite build-tooling skill group (config shape, env variables, dev proxy, plugins, build output) and an existing-codebase adoption decision skill for projects that didn't start from this plugin's own scaffold. Optionally consults a sibling codebase-map plugin for cached, checkpointed codebase facts instead of re-scanning the repo every session.
